pages.text: Snow piled up overnight. The hill and stone wall were all white.
Hungry sheep bleated in the pen. Pipo wanted to bring hay quickly. He slung a sack of hay over his shoulder.
Grandpa Sheep waved. "On snowy days, roll the hay down. That is how we always did it."
Grandpa rolled a bundle of hay across the snow. Snow stuck to it.
The bundle became a huge snowball rolling downhill. Grandpa chased it, waving his stick.
The hay was hidden; only a snowball stood at the pen. Grandpa sat down in the snow, looking like a snowman.
"Snow in the old days did not stick like this." Grandpa brushed snow off his body.
Pipo went beside the stone wall. It blocked the wind, leaving shallow snow below it.
He walked softly along the wall. Soon he reached the pen.
The sheep buried their noses in hay and munched. Grandpa stood before the snowball, gazing up. It was taller than he was.
